clue.text: Names for two men, overlapping with no name

indicators.note: two things that overlap share a stretch, so the shared letter is counted only once where they meet

blocks.note: the first man's name
the second man's name, whose first letter is shared with the end of the first

explanation.surface: Someone lists two men's names that run into each other, and ends up with no name at all.
explanation.walkthrough: GENE and ERIC share the E where they meet, giving GENERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A generic product is sold without a brand name, so generic means unbranded.

clue.text: Ruminant's mistake: eating the first rabbit's head

indicators.note: a head is at the top, so the opening letter is taken
food that is eaten goes inside, so the other parts are placed within

blocks.note: a gaffe is a social blunder
Roman numeral one, as in a monarch's title
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cud-chewing animal blunders by nibbling a rabbit's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A giraffe chews the cud, which makes it a ruminant like cattle and deer.

clue.text: Fruit in tree can burst (9)c

indicators.note: something that bursts breaks apart, letting its contents land in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a stray character after the enumeration in the source copy, not part of the clue

explanation.surface: Fruit hanging in a tree may split open.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a stone fruit.

clue.text: Undulate with a great hit on the radio after the intro

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear the word, so it is spelt as it sounds
taking what comes after the intro means losing the opening letter

blocks.note: in baseball a triple is a three-base hit

explanation.surface: A song that becomes a huge radio hit makes waves.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIPLE spoken can be spelt T-RIPPLE; drop its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripple is to move in small waves, which is what undulate means.

clue.text: Cuts up insects with utensils

blocks.note: to chop is to cut into pieces
ticks are small bloodsucking arachnids, loosely called insects

explanation.surface: Someone dissects bugs using kitchen tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopsticks are the pair of sticks used as eating implements in East Asia.

clue.text: Shorten a span

blocks.note: taken as written
a bridge spans a river or gap

explanation.surface: An instruction to make some stretch or interval shorter.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to cut it down to a shorter version.

clue.text: Snakes, as an afterthought

blocks.note: taken as written
PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: Snakes mentioned only in passing, tacked on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous Egyptian vipers, so they are snakes.

clue.text: Disavow blend of ecru neon

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters are stirred into another order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a garish paint mix of beige and neon.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce something is to give it up or formally reject it, as disavow does.

clue.text: Material taken from inside the earth, upward

indicators.note: in a down entry, going upward means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: dug out of the ground, as ore or coal is

explanation.surface: Some substance extracted from deep in the ground and brought to the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken from inside' looks like a hidden-word signal, but it is a description of mining.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is the sturdy cotton cloth used for jeans, so it is a material.

clue.text: Guaranteed goal involving deceptive ruse

indicators.note: something deceptive misleads, so the letters are disguised in another order
involving means including, so one part takes the other inside it

blocks.note: an end is an aim
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A goal that was certain to happen because of a trick play.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain, so ensured means made certain or secured.

clue.text: Summarize Indiana athlete's comeback

indicators.note: a comeback goes back the way it came, so the word is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: the Indiana Pacers are a professional basketball team

explanation.surface: Sum up the story of an Indiana player's return to form.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to go over the main points again briefly, a synonym of summarize.

clue.text: Poison-pen post on cons

indicators.note: poisoning spoils something, so the letters that follow are corrupted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spiteful anonymous letter mailed to convicts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poison-pen' reads as one adjective, but the hyphen hides a split: Poison is the signal and pen joins the letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'pros and cons' the cons are the side against, so opponents are those arguing the con side.

clue.text: Failing criminal? That's perfect

blocks.note: F is the failing grade on a school report
a criminal acts outside the law

explanation.surface: A crook who keeps messing up, and someone remarks sarcastically that it is ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawless has no defects at all, which is what perfect means.

clue.text: Three months with a computer?

blocks.note: first meaning: the season from June to August
second meaning: one who sums, an old sense of computer as a person doing arithmetic

explanation.surface: A quarter of a year spent working with a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a made-up noun: someone who adds things up, just as a computer once meant a person who calculated.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer is a season of about three months, and a summer is also anyone who adds figures.

clue.text: Liar initially trapped in difficult situations, fingered and caught unawares

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before
something trapped in a place is held inside it

blocks.note: to be in a bind is to be in a tight spot
its opening letter
fingered meaning identified, written ID'ed

explanation.surface: A liar cornered and named by witnesses is taken by surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To be blindsided is to be hit from an unexpected direction, so to be caught by surprise.

clue.text: Leave one who just tagged somebody?

blocks.note: first meaning: to go out
second meaning: in the game of tag, whoever tags another player stops being 'it', so is a former it

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as EX-IT: the tagger has just handed over the role of 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exit is a verb meaning to go out, and split as ex-it names a former 'it' in tag.

clue.text: Like an injured joint, __________ between C and E

blocks.note: first meaning: put out of its normal position
second meaning: split as ..., it completes the sentence about the alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: The blank wants a sentence about the alphabet: the answer split as D IS LOCATED fills it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dislocated shoulder or knee has come out of its socket, the typical joint injury.

clue.text: Temporary shelter lets in horrible rains

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, so the letters come out jumbled
letting something in means it ends up inside

blocks.note: a tent is a portable shelter
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A makeshift shelter that leaks in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temporary shelter' looks like one phrase for the answer; the definition is just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means passing or short-lived, the same as temporary.

clue.text: Observers' gold cube, formerly lacking face

indicators.note: a word lacking its face has lost its front, the first letter

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is a numbered cube
once means formerly

explanation.surface: The spectators' golden dice, which used to have a face missing.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is the group of people watching a performance, a collective word for onlookers.

clue.text: Exploring underground, Louis XIV clutches fur, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
something clutched is held inside a grip, so one part sits within the other

blocks.note: Louis XIV of France was known as the Sun King
a pelt is an animal's furry skin

explanation.surface: The French king going caving while holding onto a fur.
explanation.walkthrough: PEL(t) sits after the S of SUN KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelunking is the American word for the hobby of exploring caves.

clue.text: Walks all over relative

blocks.note: to step on someone is to walk all over them

explanation.surface: A family member who tramples over everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, STEPS ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is the son of one's spouse from a previous relationship, a family member by marriage.

clue.text: Exclude gravity? When a universe forms, it might be big

definitions.text: When a universe forms, it might be big

blocks.note: to ban is to exclude
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A physicist asks whether gravity can be left out of a model of how a universe starts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in: the Big ___ is the theory of how the universe began.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Bang is the cosmological event in which the universe is thought to have formed.

clue.text: Young woman circling New York neighborhood gets some fuel

indicators.note: circling something means going round it, so one part encloses the other

blocks.note: gal is informal for a girl
SoHo is a district of lower Manhattan

explanation.surface: A girl driving around SoHo stops to fill up.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasohol is a motor fuel blended from gasoline and ethanol, one particular kind of fuel.

clue.text: Pequod's chief, for example, when at large, for example!

definitions.text: Pequod's chief, for example, when at large, for example!

indicators.note: the chief of something is the one at its head, so the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: its opening letter
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
surface padding joining the parts
L is the clothing size abbreviation for large
e.g. again

explanation.surface: Captain Ahab of the Pequod, out roaming the seas, is held up as a model case.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pequod is the whaling ship in Moby-Dick, and its captain, Ahab, walked on an ivory leg, so the whole clue describes him as well as building the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Ahab is the classic example of a peg leg, a person with an artificial wooden leg.

clue.text: Direct baseball team to swallow drink in retreat

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so one part goes within the other
a retreating army goes back the way it came, so the whole is read backwards

blocks.note: a baseball team has nine players and is called a nine
OJ is American shorthand for orange juice

explanation.surface: A manager orders a ball club to down a drink as it pulls back.
explanation.walkthrough: A baseball side is called a nine because it fields nine players; OJ is American shorthand for orange juice.
explanation.definitionFit: To enjoin someone is to instruct or order them, so it means direct as a verb.

clue.text: One of twelve leaders in Jerusalem, urging right of return

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their front letters, taken from each in turn

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: An Israeli or Palestinian figure presses for the right of return to Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelve suggests the tribes or apostles of the surface; it is the size of a jury.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial jury traditionally has twelve members, so a juror is one of twelve.

clue.text: Rates female donkeys?

blocks.note: first meaning: evaluates
second meaning, a made-up word: the feminine ending -ess added to a donkey, as in lioness, then made plural

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented sense: if a female lion is a lioness, a female ass is an ass-ess.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess something is to judge its value or quality, which is to rate it.

clue.text: Whirlpool Galaxy captivates Russian woman

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the name is held inside the words

blocks.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A spiral galaxy enchants a Russian stargazer.
explanation.definitionFit: Olga is a common Russian woman's first name, so it stands for a Russian woman by example.

clue.text: Scattered equipment for winter fun around front of Philadelphia hockey arena

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter
around means surrounding, so one part wraps the others

blocks.note: a sled is used for sliding on snow
its opening letter
ice hockey is played on a rink

explanation.surface: Winter sports gear left lying about a Philadelphia ice rink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprinkled means dotted about in small amounts, a synonym of scattered.

clue.text: Feeble echo conceals parasite

indicators.note: what is concealed sits out of sight within other words

blocks.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A faint echo masks the sound of some pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking worm, the classic parasite, and the word also means someone who sponges off others.

clue.text: Latin American dictator who succeeded Enotsega and Eznorbega?

blocks.note: the two odd names are Stone Age and Bronze Age with each word written backwards; the era that followed them is the Iron Age, and this is its first word
the second word of that era's name

explanation.surface: A history question about which strongman came after two rulers with outlandish names.
explanation.walkthrough: The two names show the rule: each word of an era's name written backwards. Manuel Noriega ruled Panama in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuel Noriega was the military strongman who ran Panama until the US invasion of 1989.

clue.text: Enjoy almost everything about numbers

indicators.note: almost means falling just short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: 'dig it' is slang for enjoy it
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone likes nearly everything to do with arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital means relating to digits, the figures 0 to 9, so it concerns numerals.
